lesson_title: Enlarging and Reducing Figures on the Coordinate Plane
hook_text: The copier said 71 percent. Here is why that number halves a page exactly.
clip_script:
A teacher in Pietermaritzburg photocopies a worksheet diagram — a right-angled triangle — and the copies come out wrong in size. At 50 percent, every coordinate is halved, so every length is halved — and the area drops to a quarter, not a half.

The teacher wanted two worksheets on one page. A5 is half the area of A4, so k squared must be one half, and k is the square root of one half: about 0,71. That is the 71 percent button. The reverse, A5 to A4, is 141 percent: the square root of 2. Multiply every coordinate by k, and remember that area follows k squared.
visual_style: A photocopier panel with 50, 71 and 141 percent buttons; a triangle on a page shrinks towards the corner with its coordinates updating, and an A4 sheet folds into two A5 halves
call_to_action: Open the full session to enlarge and reduce any figure from the origin.
